rules.problem: Files are Latin-1 (not UTF-8), use ";" as delimiter, CRLF line endings and quote every field. Reading them as UTF-8 yields mojibake in every accented name.
rules.rule: Decode with TextDecoder("iso-8859-1") and assert the result has no U+FFFD and no double-encoding signature ("Ã©"-style sequences).
rules.title: ISO-8859-1 encoding, CRLF, every field quoted

rules.problem: All six value columns are strings like "13404423,26"; there is no thousands separator, but the decimal separator is a comma.
rules.rule: Parse with a strict regex into integer centavos (exact in a Float64 below 2^53). Any value that does not match the regex aborts the run instead of becoming NaN.
rules.title: Money stored as text with a decimal comma

rules.problem: The plano orçamentário code is only unique inside an action and an agency: code "0001" under action "2000" names 30 different plans in FY2025.
rules.rule: Plano orçamentário is keyed by (órgão subordinado, ação, código PO); the dictionary entry points to its parent action.
rules.title: "Código Plano Orçamentário" is not a key

rules.problem: Committed, verified and paid amounts can be negative in a month: they are reversals (estornos) of earlier commitments, not errors.
rules.rule: Kept as-is. Dropping or clamping them would overstate execution; the UI shows the sign and monthly cumulative series absorb them.
rules.title: Negative amounts

rules.problem: A budget line can appear in a month with every amount equal to zero (nothing committed, paid or carried over). It adds a row and no information.
rules.rule: Drop the row and count it. This is the only rule that drops rows; the count is asserted in validation (input = kept + dropped).
rules.title: Rows where all six values are 0,00

rules.problem: Nothing in the file says whether a month's values are the month's movement or the cumulative position. They are deltas: January 2025 alone shows R$1.76T committed (annual payroll and debt are committed up front), later months show only what changed.
rules.rule: Sum months to get the year; compute cumulative series in the aggregation step. Documented because a YTD reading would over-count twelvefold.
rules.title: Monthly files are deltas, not year-to-date
